katie-sales: Heads-up — Medisync signed a verbal 12‑month commit. They're targeting ~500k tokens/day, with two traffic peaks: 10k reqs/hr during business hours and a nightly batch of heavy summarization. POC starts Mon. They asked for: recommended reserved GPU sizing, an autoscale policy for burst windows, and answers for the security questionnaire (KMS/HSM, VPC egress). Can eng/ops give a short sizing + prewarm plan and rough pricing to put in the contract? cc @jason-ssdeng @maria-mlsre

jason-ssdeng: quick clarifying q — what's their avg seq len and p95 latency requirement? sizing depends a lot on those. Do they need realtime <200ms or user-facing <500ms?

katie-sales: They said user-facing chat at p95 <= 400ms for short responses (avg 64 tokens) and async summarization can take up to 2s (avg 1024 tokens). Peak concurrency estimate: business hours ~120 concurrent, nightly batch ~30 concurrent long jobs.

maria-mlsre: Ok. Rough calc: for the short-chat profile (64 tokens, 400ms p95), one A100-80 GPU with our optimized VM does ~1.4k tokens/s in steady state for the chosen model variant—so for peak chat (assume 2 req/s per user) we'd need ~2-3 GPUs reserved to hit latency SLO with headroom. Night summarization (1024 tokens, 2s) is CPU/GPU heavy but lower concurrency; add 1-2 transient burst GPUs or rely on autoscale.

sam-ops: My recommendation: reserved pool = 4 x A100-80 (gives safe headroom + room for node maintenance). Autoscale policy to add up to +3 spot/AZ burst nodes for 15‑minute windows. Prewarm KV cache during business hours with a rolling warm job 10m before peak.

jason-ssdeng: I can give a compact config snippet for autoscale + prewarm. Paste into the proposal appendix so SRE team can review.

```yaml
autoscale:
  reserved: 4
  max_burst: 7
  burst_policy:
    cooldown: 900  # seconds
    trigger: qps > 80 for 2m
prewarm:
  kv_warm: true
  schedule: "cron(*/10 13-18 * * MON-FRI)" # ten minutes before expected peak
```

maria-mlsre: Pricing note: reserved 4 A100-80 + expected burst usage (est 10% of monthly tokens) moves them into the obvious discount band. For a proposal number, I'll send a conservative estimate: reserved flat + per-token for burst. Katie, include a clause for "quantized model variant" fallback if spot capacity unavailable.

katie-sales: Thanks — also security Qs from their infosec: need KMS integration (customer-managed key), VPC peering with egress restrictions, and audit logs retention 1y. Are those gated for Private or doable in Dedicated?

sam-ops: KMS + VPC peering + audit logs (1y) = OK on Dedicated with the private control plane. For Hosted we'd need legal + infra exceptions. We'll note recommended path: Dedicated or Private depending on formal contract. I'll raise a short checklist for sales appendix.

jason-ssdeng: One more operational blocker: how do we handle model fallbacks if reserved pool is degraded? Suggest automatic routing to a quantized compatible variant in another AZ with degraded SLOs captured in the appendix.

katie-sales: Great — next steps: Jason, drop the autoscale YAML into the deck and add a 1-paragraph fallback behavior. Maria, send a short sizing & pricing blurb (reserved + estimated burst token cost). Sam, add the Dedicated vs Hosted security checklist. I’ll consolidate and share with Medisync legal tomorrow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Preheat job scheduled: prewarm-kv-job for Medisync POC runs at 2026-03-28T12:50Z.
